title: Noncompact Torus Localization in Equivariant Borel–Moore Homology

items.title: Localized torus-equivariant Borel–Moore classes
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $r\geq 0$, let $T=(\mathbb C^\times)^r$ act algebraically on a separated finite-type complex variety $X$, and suppose $X$ has a finite cover by $T$-invariant affine open subvarieties. Use rational coefficients. Let $K=(S^1)^r$ be the maximal compact subgroup of $T$, and use the product right Milnor model $E_K=(E_{S^1})^r$, $B_K=E_K/K=(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^r$. The inclusion $K\subset T$ gives the same topological Borel construction up to homotopy. For each algebraic character $\chi:T\to\mathbb C^\times$, let $L_\chi=E_K\times_K\mathbb C_{\chi|_K}\to B_K$, with right equivalence $(e,z)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,\chi(t)^{-1}z)$, and put $u_\chi=c_1(L_\chi)$. For the coordinate characters $\chi_i$ and $u_i=u_{\chi_i}$, the coefficient ring is $R_T=H^*(B_K;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q[u_1,\ldots,u_r]$, with $|u_i|=2$ and $u_\chi=\sum_i n_i u_i$ for $\chi(t_1,\ldots,t_r)=\prod_i t_i^{n_i}$. Let $S_T$ be the multiplicative set consisting of $1$ and finite products of $u_\chi$ for nontrivial $\chi$.

Let $H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(X;\mathbb Q)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_{T,c}(X;\mathbb Q)}(\mathbb Q_X,\omega_X^T[-j])$, where $\omega_X^T$ is the normalized equivariant dualizing object whose restriction is the ordinary dualizing object $\omega_X$, without a quotient-stack dimension shift. Equivalently, this is the stable value in degree $j$ of $H^{\mathrm{BM}}_{j+2rm}(X_m;\mathbb Q)$, where $U_m=(\mathbb C^{m+1}\setminus\{0\})^r$ has the free right scalar $T$-action, $X_m=(U_m\times X)/T$ uses $(e,x)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,t^{-1}\cdot x)$, and the supplied bounded-Hom comparison is taken in its stable range. The ring $R_T$ acts by pullback from $B_K$ and cap product. For an $R_T$-module $M$, $S_T^{-1}M$ consists of fractions $m/s$ with $m\in M$, $s\in S_T$, and $m/s=m'/s'$ exactly when some $t\in S_T$ satisfies $t(s'm-sm')=0$; addition and scalar multiplication are the induced fraction operations. Proper equivariant maps induce degree-preserving pushforwards, invariant open inclusions induce Borel–Moore restrictions, and a smooth pure $d$-dimensional complex variety has its complex-oriented fundamental class $[X]_T$ in degree $2d$. For $r=0$, $R_T=\mathbb Q$ and $S_T=\{1\}$.

items.title: Nonzero eigenfunctions annihilate equivariant BM on their nonvanishing loci
items.statement: Let $T=(\mathbb C^\times)^r$ act algebraically on a separated finite-type complex variety $X$ with a finite invariant affine open cover. Let $U$ be one affine chart, let $f\in\mathcal O(U)$ be regular with a nontrivial character $\chi:T\to\mathbb C^\times$, and fix the convention $f(t\cdot x)=\chi(t)f(x)$. If $D(f)=\{x\in U:f(x)\neq0\}$ is nonempty, then the equivariant character class $u_\chi=c_1(L_{\chi|_K})$ acts by zero on every group $H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(D(f);\mathbb Q)$. It also acts by zero on every such group for a further $T$-invariant open subvariety $V\subseteq D(f)$. Consequently $S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(D(f);\mathbb Q)=S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(V;\mathbb Q)=0$ for all $j$.

items.title: BM concentration from a finite invariant affine atlas
items.statement:
Let $T=(\mathbb C^\times)^r$ act algebraically on a separated finite-type complex variety $X$ that admits a finite cover by $T$-invariant affine open subvarieties. Let $F=X^T$ be the fixed-point subscheme, $i:F\hookrightarrow X$ its closed inclusion, and let $S_T$ be the character multiplicative set in the localized equivariant Borel–Moore definition. Then in every homological degree $j$, proper pushforward induces an isomorphism
$$
i_*:S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(F;\mathbb Q)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(X;\mathbb Q).
$$
No compactness of $X$, normality hypothesis, or compact-orbit-type nilpotence hypothesis is required.

items.title: Fixed-embedding BM self-intersection and Euler units
items.statement:
Let $T=(\mathbb C^\times)^r$ act algebraically on a smooth separated finite-type complex variety $X$ with a finite invariant affine open cover. Let $F=X^T$, $i:F\hookrightarrow X$, and $\nu_F=TX|_F/TF$ be the complex normal bundle. Then $F$ is smooth, $T_xF=(T_xX)^T$ for every $x\in F$, and every normal fiber has only nontrivial $T$-weights. On each fiber the restriction of $e_T(\nu_F)$ to $BT$ is the product of the corresponding character classes with multiplicity. The closed regular embedding $i$ has an equivariant refined Gysin map $i^!:H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(X;\mathbb Q)\to H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_{j-2c}(F;\mathbb Q)$ on each component of complex codimension $c$, normalized by $i^![X]_T=[F]_T$, with
$$
i^!i_*\beta=e_T(\nu_F)\mathbin{\cap}\beta
$$
for every $\beta\in H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_*(F;\mathbb Q)$, using the normalized Borel–Moore grading and complex orientation. If $F$ is proper, then $e_T(\nu_F)$ is a unit in $S_T^{-1}H_T^*(F;\mathbb Q)$. Empty components contribute no class, and a rank-zero normal bundle has Euler class $1$.

items.title: Intrinsic localized pushforward for a proper fixed locus
items.statement:
Let $T=(\mathbb C^\times)^r$ act on a smooth separated finite-type complex variety $X$ with a finite invariant affine open cover. Let $F=X^T$ be proper, $i:F\hookrightarrow X$, $p_F:F\to\mathrm{pt}$, and $S_T$ the character multiplicative set. By the finite-affine-atlas concentration isomorphism, $i_*:S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(F;\mathbb Q)\to S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(X;\mathbb Q)$ is invertible. Define the intrinsic localized pushforward
$$
p^{\mathrm{loc}}_*:=p_{F*}\circ(i_*)^{-1}:S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(X;\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(\mathrm{pt};\mathbb Q),
$$
where $p_{F*}$ is the genuine proper Borel–Moore pushforward. For a homogeneous $\alpha\in H_T^q(X;\mathbb Q)$ and smooth complex dimension $d$, an allowed insertion is $\alpha\cap[X]_T\in H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_{2d-q}(X;\mathbb Q)$; the fundamental class $[X]_T$ is the complex-oriented class, not the cohomological unit $1\in H_T^0(X;\mathbb Q)$. This construction does not define an ordinary pushforward along a nonproper map $X\to\mathrm{pt}$.

title: Noncompact Torus Localization in Equivariant Borel–Moore Homology — Examples

items.title: Affine-plane localization from BM classes
items.statement: Let $T=(\mathbb C^\times)^2$ act on $X=\mathbb C^2$ by $t\cdot(z_1,z_2)=(t_1z_1,t_2z_2)$, and let $u_1,u_2$ be the first Chern classes of the two coordinate characters in the product Borel model. The single affine chart $X$ is a finite invariant affine atlas, the fixed locus is the proper point $F=\{(0,0)\}$, and the tangent weights at that point are the two coordinate characters. Compute the intrinsic localized pushforward of the complex-oriented fundamental class; the result is $1/(u_1u_2)$.

items.title: A noncompact variety with a proper fixed component
items.statement: Let $T=\mathbb C^\times$ act on $X=\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb C$ by $t\cdot([x:y],z)=([x:y],tz)$, and give $X$ the two invariant affine charts $\{x\neq0\}\times\mathbb C$ and $\{y\neq0\}\times\mathbb C$. Its fixed locus is the proper component $F=\mathbb P^1\times\{0\}$, although $X$ is noncompact. Let $\chi(t)=t$, $u=c_1(L_{\chi|_{S^1}})$, choose $p\in\mathbb P^1$, and let $h\in H^2(\mathbb P^1;\mathbb Q)$ be the complex-oriented Gysin class of $p$, so $\int_{\mathbb P^1}h=1$. Pull $h$ back to $\alpha\in H_T^2(X;\mathbb Q)$ by the projection $X\to\mathbb P^1$. Compute the intrinsic localized pushforward of $\alpha\cap[X]_T$; it is $1/u$.

items.title: Why a nonproper fixed locus needs another theory
items.statement: Let $T=\mathbb C^\times$ act trivially on $X=\mathbb C^\times=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[z,z^{-1}]$. Then the fixed locus is $F=X$, and $F\to\mathrm{pt}$ is not proper. Here proper means finite-type, separated, and universally closed; after base change to $\mathbb A^1$ with coordinate $s$, the closed subset $\{(z,s):zs=1\}\subseteq\mathbb C^\times\times\mathbb A^1$ projects to the nonclosed subset $\mathbb A^1\setminus\{0\}$. Consequently the intrinsic localized pushforward defined using a proper fixed-locus trace has no value on $[F]_T$; this example assigns no fixed-point integral or reciprocal-Euler sum.
